solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: see 25dn.
Empty tacky sweet talk: new description of Trump?

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, so only the two end letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
to coo is to murmur soft endearments
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A satirist tries out a fresh label for Trump: hollow, tacky flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: TY plus COO plus N gives TYCOON. The question mark flags that the definition is an example rather than a dictionary gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump made his name as a wealthy property magnate, and a tycoon is exactly such a powerful business figure.

clue.text: Solution put on orifice for a sort of surgery

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing put on another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: the key to a puzzle is its solution
an orifice is an opening

explanation.surface: A medic applies some liquid treatment to a bodily opening before an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' looks like a medical liquid but means the answer to a problem, and 'orifice' is just an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyhole surgery is the everyday name for minimally invasive operations done through tiny incisions, so the answer qualifies a kind of operation.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) Victory line, maybe, such as May's shelved grammar school plan?

definitions.text: such as May's shelved grammar school plan

parts.note: HMS Victory was the vessel carrying Nelson as admiral at Trafalgar, the lead vessel of his fleet
a party line

explanation.surface: Was Theresa May's abandoned plan for new grammar schools ever really a winning line?
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' admits that Victory is just one example of a flagship. Theresa May, UK prime minister, dropped her plan to expand grammar (selective state) schools after the 2017 election.
explanation.definitionFit: A government's headline proposal is called its flagship policy, and the grammar school expansion was presented as exactly that before being dropped.

clue.text: Crusty old clot in clueless cabinet

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning a word break

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A crusty old fool sits in a cabinet of ministers who have no idea what they are doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusty old clot' reads as an insult for a doddery minister; here a clot is a clot of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the dried crust of clotted blood that forms over a healing wound, hence a crusty clot.

clue.text: Gasping to reveal someone's sexuality? Keep off the booze!

parts.note: gasping for a drink means thirsty
to out someone is to expose their sexuality publicly

explanation.surface: A tabloid gasps at a sexuality exposé, then someone is told to stop drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, 'gasping' alone means desperate for a drink, usually tea or beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry out is to stop drinking alcohol, often in a clinic, so the command matches an instruction to abstain.

clue.text: Carried by Elf, Labour leader thriving to a moderate extent

indicators.note: something carried is held inside the carrier, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an elf is a kind of fairy

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of Labour
someone thriving is doing well

explanation.surface: A Labour leader, borne along by an elf, is doing only so-so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried by' reads as the Labour leader being carried, and so it is: the elf holds the letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something went fairly well means it went reasonably, not brilliantly, which is a moderate degree.

clue.text: Screwed terrier, biting very English, fetching type

indicators.note: what bites grips something in its jaws, so one part closes round another
something screwed up is twisted and mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A mangled terrier bites something very English while another breed fetches.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TERRIER become RETRIER, and V plus E slip in before the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a gun dog bred to fetch shot game, so 'fetching type' cheekily describes the breed.

clue.text: see 27ac.
E.g. got over Trump's beginning

definitions.note: the answer just means a beginning; Trump is topical colour

indicators.note: knocked over means upset and tumbled, so these letters fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of the abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recovered from the opening days of the Trump presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got over' reads as recovered, but 'over' is the signal to rearrange EG and GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: From the get-go is an American idiom meaning from the very start, so the term names a start or outset.

clue.text: Intellectual pissed by Boris's opening argument

parts.note: intoxicated; pissed is British slang for drunk

indicators.note: an opening is where a word starts, so only its initial letter is used

parts.note: first letter of Boris
a row (rhymes with cow) is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A clever person gets drunk on Boris Johnson's first move in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang pissed means drunk, not angry, which matches HIGH. Boris is Boris Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: Highbrow describes cultured, intellectual tastes or a person with them, so it fits as an adjective or noun.

clue.text: (&13/15) All the Conservatives in a frenzy about hot replacement for shaky leader? Not very — it's in perpetual crisis

indicators.note: a replacement takes another's place, so one letter is swapped for another
a frenzy is wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
saying not to something means it is excluded, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of shaky
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: The whole Tory party panics over replacing a wobbly leader, while something else is permanently in crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' is fodder too: ALL THE CONSERVATIVES IN A, with one S swapped for H and one V removed, rearranges into the answer. The NHS is Britain's state health service.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's state-funded medical system is routinely described in the press as overstretched and in crisis, so the cryptic description identifies it.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Unreliable NATO deal negotiated to restrict cocaine

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so one piece goes around another
terms that are negotiated get haggled over and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is drug slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A flaky NATO agreement is hammered out to curb the cocaine trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unreliable' looks like a comment on the deal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on personal stories rather than systematic data, so it is regarded as not trustworthy.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Toolbox company, Germany, wants scrap

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a scrap is a bit or fragment

explanation.surface: A German toolbox manufacturer is looking for scrap metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toolbox' looks like a product; read as tool + box, with tool as slang for the male member, it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece is the pouch covering the genitals in old male dress, jokingly a box for the 'tool'.

clue.text: Make it hotter, love — quick!

parts.note: to raise the temperature, shortened to temp
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An impatient lover urges a partner to turn up the heat, fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up temp' is a casual way of saying raise the temperature, which is what making something hotter does.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-tempo describes music played at a brisk pace, so it means fast or lively in rhythm.

clue.text: Lending establishment's bound to go after dupes

indicators.note: going after means following, so the second piece is placed behind the first

parts.note: pawns are people manipulated by others
a bound is a leap or hop

explanation.surface: A bank is bound to chase people it has fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as certain to, but bound is the leap; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker lends money against goods left as security, so the shop is a place that makes loans.

clue.text: Saying "Naff image, right, covers party leader?"

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes inside another
naff means shoddy and tasteless, so the letters are botched into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of party

explanation.surface: A quote about a party leader's tacky public image and a right-wing cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for uncool or tacky. IMAGE plus R is rearranged around P.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty remark or maxim, so it is a synonym of a pithy saying.

clue.text: Red-faced, filling female top with gold

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a lid is a top for a container
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone blushes while stuffing a woman's top with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female top' looks like a blouse, but they are two pieces: F, then a lid with OR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A florid complexion is flushed and ruddy, so the adjective is a synonym of having a reddened face.

clue.text: Pissed, revealed sensitive info.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: passed confidential material to the press

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pissed' usually means drunk, but here it is the verb for urinating, matching the slang sense of to leak.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a leak is slang for urinating, and a leak is also an unauthorised disclosure of secrets to journalists.

clue.text: Tube out of action? Hush up!

parts.note: a tube is a pipe
a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: The London Underground is broken, and someone wants the news suppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway, which makes 'out of action' sound like a service closure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe down is an informal command to be quiet, exactly like telling someone to hush.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Digressive leader ultimately dawdling

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter of leader
ambling is strolling slowly

explanation.surface: A party leader wanders off topic, in the end dragging things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' wants to be its own first letter, but 'ultimately' points to its last.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling speech wanders from point to point without focus, so it is a synonym of wandering off the subject.

clue.text: (& 1dn.) One into bondage, ugly sort, may show your words to be false

definitions.text: may show your words to be false

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
to sort letters is to rearrange them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A hideous person drawn into bondage could expose your lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' reads as a type of person, but it is the instruction to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Posture, gestures and expressions often betray what someone really feels, contradicting the spoken message and exposing dishonesty.

clue.text: Sporty car produces piles over bum's inside

indicators.note: lying over something covers it, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: piles of something means lots of it

indicators.note: the inside of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is used

parts.note: middle letter of bum

explanation.surface: Driving a sports car is blamed for haemorrhoids on the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piles' looks medical, and bum is British slang for bottom; both mislead. Lotus is a British sports car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a British manufacturer of light, fast sports cars, so the make is an example of a sporty vehicle.

clue.text: (& 9ac.) Obsolete Conservative needs, er, time? Sure thing

parts.note: something obsolete
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An out-of-date Tory hesitates, asking for more time, yet sounds certain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'er' is not a hesitation but two letters taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead cert is British slang for an absolute certainty, often a horse sure to win, so it equals a sure thing.

clue.text: Angela's opportunity to stagger back?

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance

indicators.note: going back runs in the opposite direction, so the letters read from right to left

parts.note: to roll is to lurch or sway

explanation.surface: Angela Merkel gets her chance to totter back into office.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is': Angela is the answer. Angela Merkel was Germany's head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Merkel held the title of German Chancellor, the country's head of government, so Angela is one example.
